correctness.rationale: The repair changes the novelty boundary, not the move, state space, or exact statistics. I inspected both frozen checkers and their saved outputs without executing them. A separate bounded reconstruction (python3 /workspace/branches/replay3.py) built synthemes from disjoint triples, obtained all distances by Floyd–Warshall, and refined unresolved distance-signature classes to exhaust five- and six-sets. It found 0 and 32,460 resolving sets, so monotonicity rules out every smaller size. The reconstruction enumerated exact one-in/one-out changes, testing T-distance 1 for slides; the undirected counts were 403,020 and 55,440. It checked all 720 symbol permutations on distances and enumerated their exact images, reproducing the 62 orbits. BFS from every orbit representative reached every state in each graph. Weighting by orbit size reproduced jump eccentricities 7:31,740 and 8:720 (the latter one orbit), and slides 17:3,780, 18:11,040, 19:10,440, 20:7,200. Because the permutations preserve both moves, these searches suffice for all start states and establish the radii, diameters, and connectedness. This directly checks the natural S6 action without identifying it with the symplectic reduction in the other checker. The repaired files retain these definitions and this finite proof.

value.rationale: The repaired finding measures exact optimal-budget reachability on a canonical highly symmetric graph, not merely a known static census. The two natural moves both preserve global reachability without extra landmarks, but changing to edge-local slides increases the worst-case path length from eight to twenty and yields a different eccentricity spectrum. The unique jump-eccentricity-eight orbit gives a precise symmetry obstruction to reducing that bound. These are useful complete benchmarks for minimum-resolving-set reconfiguration on this graph, with no extension to other cages or budgets asserted.
